newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Basketball Australia has abolished the position of executive chairman after the resignation of Mal Speed. Speed resigned his posts at BA and the National Basketball League after accepting an offer with the Australian Cricket Board. In further changes, BA appointed Damian Keough and Damien Stenmark to the board. Page 19.

Jamie Goddard will be the first ever resident of Mt Isa to pull on a Queensland State of Origin jersey, when he plays for the Maroons at Suncorp Stadium. The 24-year-old moved to play for the Gold Coast five years ago, and despite having doubts about the move then, he now believes it has all paid off. Page 19.

Australian heavyweight jockey Simon Marshall will return to racing this weekend when he rides Poetic King in the BTC Sprint at Doomben. Marshall has been out injured since he sustained rib injuries in a car accident on Australia Cup Day in March this year. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A Sydney rugby league fan has been denied a $50,000 pay-out after the New South Wales TAB refused to pay him for a drawn result at the Tri-series final. Despite the rules not allowing a drawn result, both the Queensland and NSW TAB's allowed betting on a drawn result, and then refused to pay punters on the regulation time score. Page 48.

The Sydney United soccer team will go into this weekend's grand final in Brisbane more determined than ever to win. With threats of expulsion coming this week from Soccer Australia over last week's spectator brawl at the preliminary final, the Puma's want to prove that Soccer Australia cannot ruin their team morale. Page 47.

Stacy Dragila, an American from northern California, is seen as the closest threat to 22-year-old Australian pole-vaulter Emma George, after she broke five US records in five weeks. Dragila defeated George in Paris in March to become the event's first indor world-champion, and is now setting her sights on George's records. Page 47.
THE AGE

Hawthorn Captain Jason Dunstall hopes to play one more season in the Australian Football League, despite the fact he may have to undergo a second knee reconstruction within eight months. Dunstall is undergoing exploratory surgery on his left knee today, and will then know his future. Page B20.

Collingwood is working on a relocation plan, that will see the Magpies play many of its matches in Sydney after the 2000 Olympics. It is believed the Magpies want to limit the number of grounds they play on in one season, and they also want to tap into the Sydney supporter base. Page B20.

The cricket match between the Australian one-day side and Chester-le-Street that was to played today has been abandoned due to rain, meaning former test player Michael Slater will have to wait until Thursday to make his long-awaited return to international cricket. Slater made two half centuries for Australia the last time he played in a one-dayer in India last year. Page B19.
THE HERALD SUN

World champion aerial skier Kirsty Marshall will get to show her home crowd her skills when she showcases her talents at Australia's first freestyle World Cup at Mt Buller. The Victorian resort and Ski Australia secured the event to take place at the new 400,00 facility from August 1 this year. Page 70.

Sydney Swans coach Rodney Eade expects five of his injured players to return to the side to play Collingwood on Saturday night at the SCG. Among the returnees is full forward star Tony Lockett. After two straight losses, the Swans have slipped to 13th place on the Australian Football League ladder. Page 69.

Australia will go in to the one-day international series in England under-prepared after the wash-out of yesterday's last limited overs warm-up match. To add to their woes, star batsman Greg Blewett is expected to miss the first match in Leeds, with a recurring knee injury. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Super league chief Ian Frykberg and ARL boss Neil Whittaker, have held the first meeting of the rival league competitions since News Limited's Ken Cowley and the Australian Football League's Ken Arthurson met 18 months ago. However, neither of the men will confirm attending the meeting that was held last Friday in Sydney. Page76.

Australia was on target yesterday for an upset win over the United States in the World Team Cup tournament. The result of the event rests on the doubles match between Australia's Woodbridge and Woodforde, and the US pair, O'Brien and Starke. Page 74.

The Australian women's basketball team, the Opal's, have scored a 5-0 win over Russia in the women's basketball Test series that ended in Melbourne on Monday. The Opal's thrashed Russia in the last match of the series 81-62, and are now confident going into the world championship qualifying round against New Zealand next month. Page 70.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
